title: Nobody Hit DARPA's Four-to-One Drone Lift
description: At DARPA's first Lift Challenge in August 2026, no team completed the course at the four-to-one payload-to-weight goal. AVIDrone won with 3.84 to one. A Texas A&M student team showed why it is hard: its battery was over half of the drone's weight.
series: This Week in Drones and AI

beats.text: Can a drone carry four times its weight?
beats.vo: Could a drone lift four times its own weight and still fly a course?

At DARPA's first Lift Challenge, nobody finished the course at four to one. Winner A V I Drone reached three point eight four to one. Texas A and M's entry showed the problem: its battery was over half the drone's weight, and unlike fuel, it never gets lighter.
Follow for a daily dose of engineering.

caption:
Nobody hit 4:1. 🚁
At DARPA's first Lift Challenge (Aug 2026) no team completed the course at four times drone weight. AVIDrone won with 3.84:1. Texas A&M's student drone: battery > half its weight, and unlike fuel it never gets lighter.
Next round: 4:1 is the minimum, over a longer course.
